newsitem.title: USA: NYC sees no threat from lawsuit over new agency.
newsitem.headline: NYC sees no threat from lawsuit over new agency.

text.p: New York City's budget director on Thursday saw no threat from a lawsuit filed by two state residents challenging Albany's decision to create a new financing authority for the city.

"It's a nuisance lawsuit from a gadfly who consistently harrasses the state government over bonding-related items and consistently loses. I believe that his lawsuit is without merit," said Joseph Lhota, the city budget director.

The suit was filed earlier this week in the Supreme Court of Albany by taxpayer activists Robert Schulz and Gary Loughrey. They claimed the suit over the New York City Transitional Finance Authority violates several provisions of the state constitution, including a requirement that voters approve such debt as well as rules setting the city's debt limit.
Schulz predicted the legal challenge would win easily.

"This case is a piece of cake," he told Reuters in a telephone interview, explaining the main challenge centers around the state-imposed cap on how much general obligation debt New York City can issue. The limit is fixed at 10 percent of the five-year average of real estate prices.

The temporary borrowing arm was set up in February to allow New York City to sidestep the cap, which would have crimped the city's ability to sell general obligation bonds as the built-in lag fails to fully reflect the rebound in retail estate prices since a sharp, local recession in the early 1990s.

New York City is going full steam ahead with the new authority, as Lhota said it is planning to pick underwriters for its first debt sale, which is expected in August or September, as soon as Friday or early next week.
